          Findings and Recommendations

Finding 1: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 2.5 active sessions, 21.05% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .81 active sessions, 6.85% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 8as8s1k2fhhqb.
         BEGIN PKG_CBVER02_FRDRTGSFL.READ_FILES(:1,:2,:3,:4,:5); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 1% for SQL execution,
      1% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 98% for Java execution.
   Rationale
      Waiting for event "OJVM: Generic" in wait class "Other" accounted for
      97% of the database time spent in processing the SQL statement with
      SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb".

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .79 active sessions, 6.69% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "7dgg6wsgj2w26".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 7dgg6wsgj2w26.
         INSERT /*+ APPEND NOLOGGING */  INTO GLBAJIT.TMPFDAYSTART2
         (AC_TYPE,ACMASTCODE,AC_NO,BAL,BALANCE)
         SELECT A.AC_TYPE,A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_NO,SUM(NVL(B.DEBIT,:"SYS_B_00")-NV
         L(B.CREDIT,:"SYS_B_01")) AS BAL,:"SYS_B_02" AS BALANCE
         FROM GLBAJIT.TMPFDAYSTART1 A, ACBK B
         WHERE A.ACMASTCODE=B.ACMASTCODE AND A.AC_NO=B.AC_NO
         AND  A.AC_TYPE=B.AC_TYPE AND  B.AC_TYPE IN
         (:"SYS_B_03",:"SYS_B_04",:"SYS_B_05",:"SYS_B_06",:"SYS_B_07",:"SYS_B_
         08") AND A.AC_TYPE IN
         (:"SYS_B_09",:"SYS_B_10",:"SYS_B_11",:"SYS_B_12",:"SYS_B_13",:"SYS_B_
         14")
         AND B.TDATE<TO_DATE(:"SYS_B_15",:"SYS_B_16")
         AND NVL(B.POST,:"SYS_B_17")=:"SYS_B_18" AND
         NVL(B.CNCLED,:"SYS_B_19")=:"SYS_B_20"
         GROUP BY A.AC_TYPE,A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_NO
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 99% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      Top level calls to execute the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID
      "c5r9azshqnpvk" are responsible for 100% of the database time spent on
      the INSERT statement with SQL_ID "7dgg6wsgj2w26".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID c5r9azshqnpvk.
         BEGIN PKG_CBVER02_FDAYSTART.BANK_DAYSTART(:1,:2,:3,:4,:5); END;

   Estimated benefit is .6 active sessions, 5.04% of total activity.

   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the SELECT statement with SQL_ID
      "guhxcaf5jr0px".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID guhxcaf5jr0px.
         SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT
         ACMASTCODE,AC_CODE,AC_NAME,MAC_NAME,AC_NO,GMST_CODE,NAME,MNAME,INST_D
         ATE,INST_AMT AS AMOUNT,ADDR,MADDR,RTALUKA,MTALUKA,CITY,MCITY,
         PERIOD,P_UNIT,AC_STRT_DT,OPN_BAL,C_BAL,DEBIT,CREDIT
         FROM
         (
         SELECT A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_CODE,A.AC_NAME,A.MAC_NAME,L.AC_NO,L.GMST_COD
         E,K.NAME,K.MNAME,L.AC_DUE_DT,
         NVL(L.INST_AMT,:"SYS_B_00") INST_AMT,B.PEND_INST PEND_AMT,
         ADD_MONTHS(L.INST_DATE,C.SRNO*NVL(L.INST_PRD,:"SYS_B_01"))  AS
         INST_DATE,K.ADDR,K.MADDR,
         K.RTALUKA,K.MTALUKA,K.CITY,K.MCITY,L.PERIOD,L.P_UNIT,L.AC_STRT_DT,L.O
         PN_BAL,L.C_BAL,L.DEBIT,L.CREDIT,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY L.ACMASTCODE,L.AC_NO ORDER BY C.SRNO DESC)
         AS RNO
         FROM ACMAST A ,LNMAS L,LNACCINTMAS B,(SELECT LEVEL AS SRNO FROM DUAL
         CONNECT BY LEVEL<=:"SYS_B_02") C,BANKMAS K
         WHERE A.SUB_TYPE = :"SYS_B_03"
         AND A.AC_TYPE = :"SYS_B_04"
         AND A.ACMASTCODE = L.ACMASTCODE
         AND L.ACMASTCODE = B.ACMASTCODE
         AND L.AC_NO = B.AC_NO
         AND L.GMST_CODE = K.GMST_CODE
         AND NVL(L.POST,:"SYS_B_05") = :"SYS_B_06"

         AND NVL(B.PEND_INST,:"SYS_B_09") > :"SYS_B_10"
         AND ADD_MONTHS(L.INST_DATE,C.SRNO*NVL(L.INST_PRD,:"SYS_B_11"))
         BETWEEN  :"SYS_B_12" AND :"SYS_B_13"
         )
         WHERE RNO=:"SYS_B_14" )

Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.82 active sessions, 16.2% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.82 active sessions, 16.2% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.03 active sessions, 9.2% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.03 active sessions, 9.2% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.03 active sessions, 9.2% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "300" during the
      analysis period.
